terms.definition: Computer programs that can write, talk and make pictures that seem made by a person.
terms.example: RCMP in Alberta warn that scammers now use AI to copy voices, make fake videos and run chatbots that keep a fake romance going.
terms.what_to_do: Judge a message by what it asks you to do, not by how real it looks or sounds. If it wants money, secrecy or speed, check first.

terms.definition: A fake video, photo or recording made by AI to look or sound like a real person.
terms.example: Deepfake videos of Prime Minister Mark Carney have been used in online ads to push fake investment platforms.
terms.what_to_do: Don't trust an investment ad because a famous face is in it. Check the firm at aretheyregistered.ca before you send any money.

terms.definition: A copy of someone's voice made by AI from a short recording, used to say things they never said.
terms.example: Canadians lost nearly $3 million to family-emergency scams in 2024, some using cloned voices. A 2024 survey found 27% of Canadians had received a deepfake scam call.
terms.what_to_do: Hang up and call the person back on a number you already have. Think about a family code word that only you know.

terms.definition: A message pretending to be from someone you trust, to get your money or personal details. Smishing is the text-message version.
terms.example: Fake CRA texts say a tax refund is waiting as an Interac e-Transfer. The CRA does not send refunds that way.
terms.what_to_do: Don't tap links in surprise messages. Go to the real website by typing the address yourself, or use the organization's app.

terms.definition: Faking the name or number that shows on your phone, so a call looks like it comes from your bank or the police.
terms.example: In "bank investigator" scams, callers pose as bank staff and ask you to help catch a dishonest employee. Canadians lost over $28 million this way in 2025.
terms.what_to_do: Don't trust the name on the screen. Hang up and call the number on the back of your bank card.

terms.definition: A fake warning that your computer has a problem, so you call a "helper" who takes your money or controls your computer.
terms.example: Fake pop-ups lock the screen and show a number to call. Microsoft says its real warnings never include a phone number.

example_sources.label: Microsoft: Protect yourself from tech support scams

terms.what_to_do: Never call the number on a pop-up. Close the browser, or restart the device if it won't close.

terms.definition: A call or message pretending a family member is in trouble and needs money fast.
terms.example: Police in Newfoundland and Labrador warned in June 2025 of calls where a "grandchild" needs bail and a courier comes to collect the cash.
terms.what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or their parents. Police and lawyers never send a courier to pick up bail money.

terms.definition: Letting someone control your computer or phone from far away. Only allow it for help you asked for.
terms.example: Fake support callers ask you to install a program so they can "fix" a virus, then take money or personal details.

example_sources.label: Microsoft: Protect yourself from tech support scams

terms.what_to_do: Only give access to someone you contacted yourself. If a stranger got in, turn off the internet, call your bank, and get the device checked.
